Close QA-Pair Generation

In the task of QA-pair generation given a context we need to generate all possible question context pairs that can be generated. Each context provides information which can be turned into questions whose answer is present in itself. QA-Pair generation can be solved using an encoder-decoder model. The whole context is given as input to the encoder which is used to generate a question and its paired answer.

Let’s look into the model architecture part now.

The model architecture consists of many layers of stacked LSTMs, 1 layer of CNN, max pooling layer. The bidirectional encoder and decoder layers contain LSTM cells. The encoder here, is a bidirectional LSTM layer whose one side takes the input data and generates a new state. It passes the output to a max pooling layer which in turn, provides an input to a CNN layer. The decoder side is again a bidirectional LSTM, with its one side passing the target answer data. The other side of the decoder includes two layers of feed-forward networks. The decoder has one-to-many mapping, which means it will generate multiple questions by taking a particular answer as input.

Support Set Learning can be used to rank the generated result. The main focus should be on Quality since redundancy is not a primary concern in the QA-pair generation model. Further, the entire process is self-monitoring in nature, and denies the need for any external support for superior performance.

In the first, Ben plays chicken with a Polacks, in the second, Mike Spark drinks beer out of engine oil filters (price of fallen wood).  Mark has a tuition in the city, where cowboys ride up and-down on their rough and matronly horses in the window display of suburban boutiques.  His sister Anna is a Domme, a blonde martinet in her white mask and sinewy leotard. She takes orders and follows rules, and her quilt of restraints is integral to bedroom, like the poem to her mother - once a Russian housekeeper, on her wedding veil - that she must now read to please her dad.  Even her 'pantyhose do not allow room for toes', and her wires are arranged spanning the inside of her thighs, like 'dental floss, lodged between molar and gum', and rarity traded in the backstreets of a Greek Orthodox summer village.
